title: World Models for Embodied Intelligence: From Plausible to Controllable to Actionable
abstract: arXiv:2609.16697v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: World models connect perception and decision-making in embodied intelligence by maintaining hidden state, anticipating consequences, comparing interventions, and adapting when execution departs from expectations. Although progress is often measured by visual fidelity, their value lies in improving behavior. Before reaching for a cup, a person anticipates its weight and resistance to grasping, shaping the hand before contact. Such anticipation is coarse and rarely pictorial, yet it guides action. This raises a central question: which predictive capabilities improve behavior? Existing surveys, organized by architecture, output modality, or application domain, leave this question implicit. translated_title: 具身智能的世界模型：从合理到可控再到可行动
translated_abstract: 世界模型通过维护隐状态、预判后果、比较不同干预措施以及在执行偏离预期时进行自适应调整，将具身智能中的感知与决策连接起来。尽管该领域的研究进展通常以视觉保真度来衡量，但世界模型的真正价值在于改进行为。在伸手拿杯子之前，人会预先估计杯子的重量和抓取阻力，从而在接触之前就调整手部姿态。这种预判是粗略的、很少是图像化的，却能有效地指导行动。这引出了一个核心问题：哪些预测能力能够真正改进行为？现有的综述往往按架构、输出模态或应用领域进行组织，并未明确回答这一问题。我们提出了三个能力逐级增强的层次：合理模型保留与任务相关的时序、几何或物理结构；可控模型在此基础上进一步预测干预措施如何改变该结构；可行动模型则……（原文摘要不完整）
tldr: 本文提出评估具身智能世界模型的三级递进能力框架——合理、可控、可行动，指出世界模型的价值不在于视觉保真度，而在于识别哪些预测能力能真正改进行为。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a three-level progressive capability framework for evaluating world models in embodied intelligence—Plausible, Controllable, and Actionable—arguing that the value of world models lies not in visual fidelity but in identifying which predictive capabilities genuinely improve behavior.
